data.name: Rishinath
data.gender_notes: Rishinath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Rishinath is a name derived from Sanskrit and is commonly used in Hindu culture. It is believed to mean 'God's protection' or 'God's grace'. This name is often given to boys as a sign of devotion and faith. The name Rishinath carries the meaning “God's protection, God's grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Rishinath usually hope their child will grow to embody god's protection, god's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine protection and blessings of the gods.
data.etymology: Rishinath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's protection, God's grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rishinath total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rishinath carries immense cultural significance as it is considered a sacred name derived from Sanskrit. In Hindu culture, it is believed that the gods protect their devotees and bestow their blessings upon them. Naming a child Rishinath is a way of invoking the gods' protection and grace upon the child, instilling in them a sense of spiritual connection, faith, and respect for the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rishinath holds great spiritual significance as it symbolizes the belief in divine protection and grace. This name is a reminder that a higher power is always looking out for us, guiding us, and offering us strength, courage, and wisdom. It is a name that inspires faith, devotion, and a deep connection with the divine. Naming a child Rishinath is a way of passing down this essence of faith and devotion from generation to generation, instilling in them a sense of spiritual power and resilience.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rishinath: Seeker of Enlightened Masters (Rishis) Path illuminated by the guidance of wise sages.

vedic_reference.note: Rishinath is a name of Vedic deity Rishabh or Rishabha, who is the first Jyotirlinga, the first Tirthankara, and the first king of the world according to Hindu scriptures. He is considered as the embodiment of Dharma and is also known as Vibhishana-Rishabh. Rishinath is also considered as the Adi-Guru, the first teacher. He is often depicted as a bull, symbolizing strength and stability.

historical_references.reference: Rishinath was a renowned Jain scholar and philosopher of the 13th century AD who contributed significantly to the development of Jain philosophy and literature. He wrote several commentaries on various Jain texts, including the Nyayavishaya and the Tattvartha Sutra.

Rishinath was also known as Rishabhanatha III, as he was the thirteenth leader of the Digambara Jain sect in the Bhagavati tradition. He ruled over the kingdom of Mysore in present-day Karnataka, India, around the 14th century AD, and was a patron of Jainism.
